title: "Benchmark Results"
---

## Overview

The GRI has been benchmarked against two major global survey programs:

- **[Global Dialogues](https://global-dialogues.ai/)** --- A longitudinal survey series capturing public perceptions of AI, deliberately designed for global demographic representation (~1,000 participants per wave from 50+ countries).
- **[World Values Survey](https://www.worldvaluessurvey.org/)** --- The largest global social survey program, running since 1981, with ~58,000 participants per wave across 60--100 countries.

These two programs represent different design philosophies: Global Dialogues prioritizes demographic balance with smaller samples, while WVS prioritizes broad geographic reach with large convenience samples. Comparing them reveals that **survey design matters more than sample size** for representativeness.

## GD vs. WVS Comparison

![Global Dialogues achieves higher GRI scores across all dimensions despite having 1/58th the sample size. Precision retention shows the cost of demographic mismatch.](images/gd_vs_wvs_comparison.png){.figure width="100%"}

### Key Takeaways

- **Deliberate design outperforms convenience sampling.** GD achieves 40--70% higher GRI on intersectional dimensions with ~1,000 participants vs. WVS's ~58,000.
- **WVS's size advantage is consumed by reweighting.** On Country x Religion, WVS averages a design effect of 29.4, meaning ~58,000 respondents yield the precision of ~3,600.
- **Both surveys struggle with intersectional precision.** Even GD retains only 10--34% of its nominal precision on primary dimensions---the combinatorial challenge of matching multiple distributions simultaneously is inherent.
- **GD3 consistently outperforms** despite having the smallest sample (N = 971), confirming that recruitment strategy matters more than sample size.
- **Age representation improves steadily** in GD---a trend from 0.66 (GD1) to 0.76 (GD6) suggests iterative refinement.

## Sampling Efficiency

Raw GRI scores can be misleading without context. A score of 0.35 on Country x Gender x Age sounds low, but the maximum achievable score at N = 1,000 is only 0.79. **Efficiency ratios** normalize scores against these theoretical ceilings:

| Dimension | Max GRI (N=1000) | GD Avg. Actual | Efficiency |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Country x Gender x Age | 0.792 | 0.344 | 43% |
| Country x Religion | 0.938 | 0.502 | 54% |
| Country x Environment | 0.950 | 0.421 | 44% |

GD achieves 43--54% of the theoretical maximum across primary dimensions, indicating room for improvement through targeted recruitment while capturing a meaningful share of achievable representativeness.

## Compare Your Survey

The GRI framework can be applied to any survey with demographic data. See the [Python library documentation](library.qmd) to calculate GRI scores, design effects, and effective sample sizes for your own data.
